_comment: Registry of temporary workarounds in this flake. Every entry has a matching `WORKAROUND(<id>)` tag at each site listed in `files`. Check contract: `command` exits 0 = fixed, 1 = still needed, anything else = check error. Run a check from the repo root with NIXPKGS="path:$(nix eval --raw .#nixosConfigurations.zephyrus.pkgs.path)" NIXPKGS_SRC="$(nix eval --raw .#nixosConfigurations.zephyrus.pkgs.path)" REPO="$PWD" bash -c '<command>'. A good moment to run them is after a flake update. When one reports fixed, follow its `remove` text.

workarounds.title: asus-shutdown.service is not restarted/stopped on switch
workarounds.reason: asusctl ships asus-shutdown.service with SendSIGKILL=no and the daemon defers SIGTERM until real shutdown, so nixos-rebuild's restart-on-switch times out and the switch exits non-zero.

check.command: unit="$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths "$NIXPKGS#asusctl")/lib/systemd/system/asus-shutdown.service" || exit 2; if ! grep -q '^SendSIGKILL=no' "$unit"; then exit 0; fi; grep -q 'restartIfChanged' "$NIXPKGS_SRC/nixos/modules/services/hardware/asusd.nix" && exit 0; exit 1

workarounds.remove: Delete the systemd.services.asus-shutdown block from modules/laptop/rog.nix and its README known-issues entry, then dry-build. Test with `sudo nixos-rebuild test --flake .#zephyrus` twice in a row: the second activation must not fail on asus-shutdown.

workarounds.title: Keyboard LED mode and brightness re-sent to asusd after resume
workarounds.reason: asusd's AuraZbus::start_tasks has its create_tasks call commented out, so the handler that restores keyboard LEDs on wake never runs and the keyboard can stay dark after suspend.

check.command: s="$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths "$NIXPKGS#asusctl.src")" || exit 2; f="$s/asusd/src/aura_laptop/trait_impls.rs"; test -f "$f" || exit 2; grep -q '// task.create_tasks(signal_ctx).await' "$f" && exit 1; exit 0

workarounds.remove: Delete auraReapply and powerManagement.resumeCommands from modules/laptop/rog.nix and the README known-issues entry. Test several suspend/resume cycles: `journalctl -u asusd | grep CtrlKbdLedTask` must show asusd's own restore running and the keyboard must stay lit.

workarounds.title: ACPI table adds the missing _PRW on LID0 so lid and power button wake s2idle
workarounds.reason: On BIOS GU603VI.317 lid and power button events reach the OS through GPE 0x02 (_L02 -> ECLV -> LEVN -> LGPA), but \_SB.PC00.LPCB.LID0 has no _PRW and nothing else claims that GPE for wake. Linux leaves it unarmed in s2idle, so only USB input such as the internal keyboard can wake the laptop. Other events share that path, so unplugging the charger now wakes the laptop too.
workarounds.remove: After a BIOS update, read the firmware's table first: `sudo cat /sys/firmware/acpi/tables/DSDT > dsdt.dat`, then `nix shell nixpkgs#acpica-tools -c iasl -d dsdt.dat`, and check whether Device (LID0) under \_SB.PC00.LPCB now has a _PRW. If it does, delete acpiLidWake and boot.initrd.prepend from modules/laptop/rog.nix and the README known-issues entry. Apply with `sudo nixos-rebuild boot --flake .#zephyrus`, reboot, and test lid and power button wake.

workarounds.title: polkit-agent-helper@ sandbox opened to the IR camera for howdy
workarounds.reason: polkit 127 runs its PAM helper as a sandboxed unit (PrivateDevices=yes, DevicePolicy=strict), so pam_howdy cannot open the IR camera. Polkit prompts then fail instantly, password fallback included. nixpkgs relaxes the sandbox for u2f/yubico/fprintd/zfs, not howdy.
workarounds.remove: Delete the systemd.services."polkit-agent-helper@" block from modules/laptop/howdy.nix. Test with Howdy enabled by opening any app that asks for admin rights through polkit: face or password must be accepted.
